comment: Per-resort corrections applied by pipeline/normalize_osm.py (ADR-036). See whistler-blackcomb.overrides.json for the format. Killington (way/1228774360, Killington Resort, 12.9 km2: Killington Peak, Skye Peak, Bear Mountain, Sunrise, Snowdon, Ramshead and the Skyeship base on US 4) on its own map (the owner's rule of 2026-11-14: one map per ski area unless the areas are connected by lift or ski trail); killington-pico-v1, retired, drew it with Pico, and these are that map's Killington entries (killington-pico.overrides.json of 2026-11-12) with their reasons. Pico Mountain (way/1094586461) is a listed neighbour in resorts.json: its polygon lies 1.8 km north-west at the nearest points, joined to Killington by no lift or ski trail (each mountain has its own 2026-27 trail map, killington.com/winter-trail-map and picomountain.com/winter-trail-map, with its own ski area boundary; the Killington/Pico Interconnect on killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status is an uphill travel route, not a trail; picomountain.com/transportation-parking-and-shuttles sends guests on to Killington by The Bus), and its 7 lifts, 92 runs, 3 run areas and 11 stations in the Overpass window are left off. Every part of Killington is reached by its own lifts and trails: the Skyeship base on US 4 by the two-stage Skyeship gondola and Great Eastern down to it, Sunrise Mountain by the Sunrise Village Triple and the trails to and from Bear Mountain, all inside the map's one ski area boundary. Every named run and lift checked again on 2026-11-14 against Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf, the file of 2026-10-07; its labels are outlines with no text layer, so it was rendered at three times its size and read tile by tile; rated with the green circle, blue square, black diamond and two black diamonds, with orange terrain-park features and hatching) and its lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status: 19 lifts and 167 alpine trails rated green, blue, black or double black, 8 terrain parks, 5 uphill routes), the starting point being the combined map's check of 2026-11-12. OSM's easy, intermediate, advanced and expert are green, blue, black and double black. Where the map and the status page both rate a run they agree, and they win over OSM (where they differ, the harder stands); where OSM splits a run the map draws in sections (Ridge Run, Ovation, Conclusion, Needle's Eye, East Fall, Great Northern, Skye Hawk), OSM's pieces already carry the sections' ratings. Ratings: Catwalk - Upper to expert; High Traverse, the first 318 m of Home Run, Nivis Walk and a 60 m piece of Pipe Dream to intermediate; the top 46 m of Dream Maker Headwall to advanced; a 131 m stretch of Great Eastern to easy; The Stash's gladed line (advanced) to intermediate. Kept as OSM has them: the 165 m connector of Bittersweet to High Road, which the map draws black with a diamond (the status page rates Bittersweet's upper and lower parts blue; the harder stands); Downdraft, one expert way where the status page rates its upper part black; and Bear Trax, one 1.7 km easy way from below Killington Peak to Bear Mountain, whose upper part, from the peak past Helter Skelter, the map draws blue and the status page rates blue (Bear Trax - Upper) while the rest is green on both: OSM does not split the way there (only an 88 m top piece from Blue Heaven is intermediate), so it stays green as most of its length is (an OSM gap; a judgment call); likewise Northbrook Trail (one easy way, labelled green on the map; the status page rates its upper part blue). Parks: The Stash (both its lines), Lil' Stash and Timberline, which the map draws as terrain parks along their whole length, get the park flag. Not flagged: the parks the status page lists on trails of the same name (Easy Street Park, Mouse Run Park, Reason Park, Full House Park and Dream Maker's park), which OSM maps as the whole trail, so a park flag would draw the whole run as a park. Names from the map and the status page: Snowshed Crossover (OSM Northbrook Crossover, the crossover's lower part), Treezy (OSM Treezy Zone); lifts Superstar Six (OSM Superstar Express Six), Snowdon Quad (OSM Snowdon Triple), Snowdon Six Express (OSM Snowdon Six), Learn To Carpet (OSM Learn To Snowboard Carpet) and Progression Carpet I (OSM Snowplay Carpet I). Names that differ from the map or the status page only by a space, an apostrophe, a hyphen or a section suffix stay as OSM has them (Sundog for Sun Dog, Stash Way for STASHWAY, The North Way for The Northway, Skye Hawk for SKYEHAWK, Superpipe for Superpipe Trail, Needle's Eye for Needles Eye, Learn To Ski And Ride Area for the map's LEARN TO AREA); runs OSM names that neither source prints stay (Low Traverse, and Magic Snow Play Park at the Ramshead base). All 19 of the status page's lifts are in OSM. Hidden: Snowplay Carpet II (the map draws one carpet in that learning area), the Alpine Training Venue Poma (a race-training lift on neither source), the abandoned Devil's Fiddle and Northeast Passage chairs and a 35 m gondola stub inside the K-1 base station. Out of bounds: 15 freeride lines outside Killington's polygon, where neither the map nor the status page has a trail, which OSM rates freeride with no backcountry tag: the former Northeast Passage area's Old Sundog, Old Sunrise Trail, Old Gold Dust, Gold Dust (upper and lower), Hawkeye, Nor'easter (two) and Thunderball east of Sunrise Village, and Horn, Old Vagabond, Old Swirl, Old Timberline and two unnamed lines over the ridge west of the Ramshead and Snowdon tops. Two aerialway=yes platforms at the K-1 base are left out by the lift rule, and 134 nordic, 485 ski-touring (the Catamount Trail among them) and 6 piste:type=yes ways (Pico's) by the type rule. OSM gaps (shipped as at Palisades Tahoe): Grizzly and Ledgewood Yurt Trail (blue on both sources); OSM also maps Superstar, Ovation and Downdraft whole where the status page names their Headwall sections.

overrides.reason: Catwalk - Upper, the top of Catwalk below Killington Peak, has two black diamonds on Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf), and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) rates Catwalk - Upper double black; OSM rates it advanced. The resort's sources agree and win.

High Traverse, from the top of the North Ridge Quad across to Bear Trax, is a blue square on Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) and blue in the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status); OSM rates it easy. The resort's sources agree and win.

The first 318 m of Killington's Home Run, from Bear Trax across Cascade to Great Northern, is drawn blue with a blue square on Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf), and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) rates Home Run blue; OSM rates this piece easy (its other pieces intermediate). The resort's sources agree and win.

Nivis Walk, below the South Ridge Quad's top, is a blue square on Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) and blue in the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status); OSM rates it advanced. The resort's sources agree and win.

The top 46 m of Dream Maker Headwall, from Great Eastern, is part of the headwall that Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) labels DREAM MAKER - HEADWALL with one black diamond, and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) rates Dream Maker - Headwall black; OSM rates this piece intermediate (the rest of the headwall advanced). The resort's sources agree and win.

A 60 m piece of Pipe Dream at the South Ridge Link junction: Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) draws Pipe Dream blue along its whole length and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) rates its upper and lower parts blue; OSM rates this piece easy (the rest intermediate). The resort's sources agree and win.

A 131 m stretch of Great Eastern above the Skyeship base, a second line beside the main way: Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) draws Great Eastern green from Skye Peak to the Skyeship base and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) rates its upper and lower parts green; OSM rates this stretch intermediate. The resort's sources agree and win.

The Stash, Killington's terrain park in the woods off Skye Peak, is labelled THE STASH twice with blue squares and drawn with terrain-park features along both its lines on Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf); the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) lists The Stash as a blue trail and as a terrain park (S, M, L). OSM rates this line advanced and gladed with no park tag. The resort's sources win: blue, and the park flag.

The Stash, Killington's terrain park in the woods off Skye Peak, drawn with terrain-park features on Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) and listed as a terrain park (S, M, L) in the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status); OSM has it as a blue run with no park tag.

Lil' Stash, the small terrain park at the Ramshead base, labelled LIL STASH with a terrain-park feature on Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) and listed only as a terrain park (XS, S, M) in the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status); OSM has it as a green run with no park tag.

Timberline on Ramshead is drawn with the terrain-park hatching along its whole length and terrain-park features on Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf), and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) lists Timberline Park (S, M, L) beside the Timberline trail; OSM has it as a blue run with no park tag.

Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) labels this green line, from Great Eastern to the bottom of the Skyeship Express Gondola's second stage, SNOWSHED CROSSOVER (the lower part of the crossover from Bear Mountain), and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) lists Snowshed Crossover and no Northbrook Crossover; OSM names it Northbrook Crossover.

Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) labels this green glade at the Ramshead base TREEZY and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) lists Treezy; OSM names it Treezy Zone.

Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) labels the six-seat chair from the K-1 base SUPERSTAR SIX and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) lists Superstar Six; OSM names it Superstar Express Six.

Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) labels this chair from the K-1 base to Snowdon SNOWDON QUAD and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) lists Snowdon Quad; OSM names it Snowdon Triple.

Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) labels the bubble six-seat chair to Snowdon's top SNOWDON SIX EXPRESS and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) lists Snowdon Six Express; OSM names it Snowdon Six.

Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) labels the carpet at the Snowshed base LEARN TO CARPET and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) lists the Learn To Carpet; OSM names it Learn To Snowboard Carpet.

Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) draws one carpet in the learning area at the Ramshead base, labelled PROGRESSION CARPET I, and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) lists Progression Carpet I there; OSM maps two carpets there under the area's former names, Snowplay Carpet I and II. This one keeps its numeral as the map's carpet.

Snowplay Carpet II, the second carpet OSM maps in the former Snowplay area at the Ramshead base: Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) draws one carpet there (Progression Carpet I, way/203680472) and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) lists no other, so the resort no longer runs this one.

The Alpine Training Venue Poma beside the Alpine Training Venue trail on Ramshead: a race-training lift that Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) does not draw and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) does not list (the trail itself stays, blue on both).

The former Devil's Fiddle chair on Bear Mountain, tagged abandoned in OSM: Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) draws Devil's Fiddle as a double-black trail with no lift, and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) lists no such lift.

The former Northeast Passage chair east of Sunrise Village, tagged abandoned in OSM and outside the resort's polygon: neither Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) nor the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) has it.
An unnamed 35 m gondola way inside the K-1 Express Gondola's base station (beside its platform, way/1436473708): not a lift of its own, it would draw as a separate lift with two stations.

Old Sundog: a freeride line east of Sunrise Village, in the former Northeast Passage area, outside Killington's polygon, where Killington's 2026-27 winter trail map (killington.com/winter-trail-map, KillingtonWinterTrailMap2627.pdf) draws no trail and the resort's lifts and trails status page (killington.com/lifts-and-trails-status) lists none; OSM rates it freeride with no backcountry tag, so the rule would draw it as an in-bounds run. Drawn out of bounds by the owner's rule (backcountry lines are shown, not hidden), as Jackson Hole's and Tamarack's freeride lines beyond their boundaries.
